text:
alex: Thinking about our envelope encryption rotation approach for cross-cloud keys. Two options: auto-rotate (KMS key material rotates, server accepts new default) vs server-side rewrap of stored ciphertext. Main concern: long-lived client-side ciphertext (customers keep blobs for years) and backward compatibility. Any strong opinions?

priya: I prefer server-side rewrap for our hosted DB blobs, because we can enforce a consistent envelope header format and migrate lazily. But that requires careful RBAC and audit trail.

jordan: +1 for header versioning. If every ciphertext has a small JSON header with key_id and scheme_version we can detect stale blobs and choose rewrap path.

mike: Quick note: automatic rotation (KMS key rotation) usually keeps old key versions accessible for decrypt, but not all clouds expose easy listing/rewrap semantics. AWS has ReEncrypt, GCP has rewrap with cryptoKeyVersions. Azure Key Vault is a different model. We need a cross-cloud abstraction.

alex: Good point. Proposal: 1) Add explicit envelope header (4 fields) -> {"scheme":"redwood-env","ver":"2","kms_key":"aws:arn/..|gcp:..|az:..","key_version":"v123"}. 2) Keep previous key versions usable for N days (configurable). 3) Implement a rewrap worker for stored blobs with canary -> gradual -> full rollout.

priya: For RBAC: only a dedicated service account ("kms-rewraper") should be allowed to call ReEncrypt/rewrap APIs. No human keys. Also, require MFA to change rotation window. Audit logs must capture: requester, from_key_version, to_key_version, ciphertext_id.

jordan: Add an idempotency token to rewrap operations so retries can't cause duplicate audit entries or partial state if job restarts. Also log latency and number of rewrap failures per minute for alerting.

mike: How about backwards compatibility for clients that still expect scheme ver 1? We can keep a compatibility shim in the runtime: if header missing, treat as ver 1 and avoid auto-rewrap; surface a warning in logs and in console so customer can opt-in to migration.

alex: Exactly. We should NOT break ver 1 clients. Migration path: step 0 — detect and report count of ver1 blobs; step 1 — canary rewrap 0.1% using sampled blobs; step 2 — 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. At each step validate decrypt success across SDKs and across regions.

priya: On audit retention: for compliance we should keep rewrap/audit entries for at least 7 years? That's long. Maybe 1 year by default and extended retention as an enterprise add-on. Need security/ops input.

mike: From infra: long retention is expensive. Suggest meta retention 1 year, raw logs to cold storage (S3/nearline) on 7yr for enterprise customers. But ensure logs are tamper-evident (hash chain).

jordan: Incident scenario: if a bad key is rolled, we need rollback. Keep previous key versions active for a rollback window (e.g., 72h). Also rewrap jobs must be reversible: store original key_version in rewrap metadata until finalization.

alex: Good. For rollback mechanics: when rewrap starts, create a migration record: {ciphertext_id, from_v, to_v, status, can_rollback:true}. Only mark final when all replicas ack. If rollback requested, re-encrypt back with from_v using stored ephemeral tokens. 

priya: Test plan: unit tests + integration with AWS/GCP/Azure KMS emulators (or test projects). Add e2e test that simulates partial failure (e.g., network blip) and restarts worker to ensure idempotency.

mike: Ops checklist for rollout: create KMS keys and grant kms-rewraper principal decrypt/encrypt but explicitly deny key deletion; set CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Azure Monitor alerts for rewrap error rate > X; enable audit-bot to post summary daily to #incidents (or #security-alerts).

alex: Example envelope header snippet we should standardize on (please comment):
```json
{"scheme":"redwood-env","ver":"2","kms":"aws:arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/abcd","kv":"123"}
```
Note: kv is key version id returned by KMS (or cryptoKeyVersion in GCP). Keep header small.

jordan: Also include a short TTL field for how long the server is allowed to auto-rewrap that blob (for privacy/regulatory reasons). Maybe not default, but allow per-tenant policy.

priya: Audit log example entry we want: 
"ts","actor","action":"rewrap","from":"aws:...:v123","to":"aws:...:v124","ciphertext_id":"bucket/path/obj","status":"ok|failed","request_id":"uuid"
Keep it CSV/JSON line per event.

mike: One more: RBAC changes. We'll need an admin flow to add/remove the kms-rewraper role. Gate that behind people in SRE+Security with 2 approvers. Also record role changes in audit-bot.

alex: Ok action items: 
- Priya: draft rewrap runbook (canary percentages, rollback steps, RBAC policy) by next Wed (1782614799).
- Jordan: design envelope header spec and compatibility shim by EOD Fri.
- Mike: prototype rewrap worker with idempotency token + cloud-agnostic KMS adapter; instrument audit events.
- Alex: write a short FAQ for customers about what rotation means and how we handle old blobs.

deploy-bot: scheduled job created: kms-rewrap-canary-sample-run -> starts 1782100000 (canary) :rotating_light:

audit-bot: daily-summary will post rewrap counts to #security-alerts at 06:00 UTC starting 1782030000

priya: one more question — what's our tolerance for rewrap latency per object? If we block on re-encrypt we could spike request latency. My thought: rewrap asynchronously for reads/writes; do not block client RW paths for background migration.

jordan: Agreed. For hot paths we should decrypt with old key and return; then schedule background rewrap for that object. Add middleware metric for post-read rewrap queue length.

alex: Nice. This thread is enough for the first pass. We'll collect comments and move to a doc in confluence. If anyone has objections to storing original key_version in migration metadata (privacy or compliance concerns), flag now.

mike: No objections from infra side, but security should sign off on retention of original metadata.

priya: I'll loop in compliance after I draft the runbook.

alex: Thanks all.

ACTION_SUMMARY: ["priya: draft runbook by 1782614799","jordan: envelope header spec by EOD Fri","mike: prototype rewrap worker","alex: customer FAQ"]
